chapter_name: Silk Road by Nick Middleton & Father to Son by Elizabeth Jennings
learning_objective: 🎯 Trek across the freezing Tibetan Himalayas toward Mount Kailash, and experience the universal heartbreak of a father trying to bridge the emotional gap with his grown son!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🏔️ The Difficult Journey to Mount Kailash (Silk Road)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Nick Middleton travels along the ancient Silk Road through freezing passes, snow-blocked roads, and high altitudes (over 5,000 meters) to complete the Buddhist 'Kora' (pilgrimage around Mount Kailash).
Along the desolate plains, the author encounters 'Drokbas' (nomadic shepherds) guarded by ferocious black Tibetan Mastiffs—huge, fearless dogs that chase their car like bullets.

main_concepts.concept_title: 💔 The Silence Between Father and Son
main_concepts.simple_explanation: In Elizabeth Jennings's poem, a father laments that although he and his son have lived in the same house for years, they are complete strangers who share no understanding or communication.

The father wishes his independent son would return home like the Biblical 'prodigal son'. Even if the son makes mistakes, the father prefers forgiving him and rebuilding love rather than facing empty silence.

fun_activity.title: 💬 Break the Silence
fun_activity.instructions: In 'Father to Son', the poet writes: 'Silence surrounds us.' Think of an older relative or parent you haven't had a long chat with recently. Ask them one simple question about their own childhood today!

exam_tips: 📌 Describe the author's medical emergency in Darchen: high-altitude cold blocked his sinuses, preventing him from breathing lying down until a Tibetan doctor gave him herbal medicine.
📌 Explain the Biblical allusion of the 'Prodigal Son' used in Elizabeth Jennings's poem—the father's longing to forgive and welcome back a wayward child.
📌 Contrast the romantic expectation of Hor (a holy place near Lake Manasarovar) with its depressing reality: dirty, miserable, and littered with rubbish.
quick_recap: ⭐ The author befriended Norbu, a Tibetan working in Beijing who also wanted to complete the Kora.
⭐ 'Father to Son' is written in a deeply confessional tone, capturing universal generational conflict.
⭐ Both texts explore journeys—one a rugged physical pilgrimage through Tibet, the other an emotional search for family reconciliation.
